subject: biology

items.q: Are characteristics gained during life (like big muscles) inherited?
items.correct: No — only genetic variation is passed on.
items.why: Offspring inherit genes, not features developed through use or environment during a parent's life.

items.correct: A change in a population over many generations by natural selection.
items.misconception: An individual changing during its own lifetime.
items.random_wrong: Animals choosing to grow new features.
items.why: Evolution acts on populations across generations as advantageous inherited traits become more common.

items.correct: Random variation plus selection of advantageous traits — no intent.
items.misconception: Because they want or need to change.
items.random_wrong: Because they try hard to adapt.
items.why: Variation arises randomly; individuals better suited to the environment survive and reproduce more.

items.q: Is continuous variation (like height) controlled by a single gene?
items.correct: No — it is polygenic (many genes) and affected by environment.
items.random_wrong: It is not inherited at all.
items.why: Continuous variation results from many genes plus environmental factors; discontinuous variation is often one gene.
